title: What is distinctive in New Orleans drumming
summary: He cannot compare to other cities and says he plays by feeling.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Frog and I were talking about some of the things that make New Orleans music different than other things. Like he mentioned the melody and the fact that they get together, play together and a few other things as well. Another thing, as he said, his father told him about to be able to play any type of music. Is there anything, remarks you'd have about the particular kind of drumming that you've noticed? Any other drummers away from here that they're different than the fellows here, their beat or anything, if you could explain, have you noticed any difference in the New Orleans style of drumming you might say, compared to say the way they do up north or other places?

Well no, I have never heard any of the guys playing all this music away from here. The only time I was away from here, Bill, when I was with Artie Crossley's band, I went to Los Angeles and played out there. Oh yeah. And in fact, we were the only band, they had the bandage to play there on Sundays, but I had never went down to here. So I couldn't say anything about the guys playing drums.

Have you ever had any experience of other drummers from outside of town coming in here and trying to play with some of your bands and noticed that they played differently or? No. Anything much about, different style or anything? No, I haven't. Is there anything that you can make any remarks about the New Orleans music? Things that you try to do with your drumming?
